Here, **the soil of Israel** represents “the people who live on the soil of Israel.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to the people who live in Israel]

Yahweh is using the word **End** as an exclamation to express a strong warning of the coming disaster. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [This is it] or [It’s all over]

The implication is that the end of Israel as a nation has come, because Yahweh is about to destroy the land and its people. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. This also occurs in verse 6. Alternate translation: [Israel is finished! Destruction has come]

Yahweh is using **the four edges of the land** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the whole land.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. 3.note: Yahweh is addressing “the soil of Israel,” so the pronoun **you** is singular here and refers to the land of Israel in this verse and the next. However, he knows that soil cannot hear him, and the real audience is the people who live there. He is doing this to communicate to the people that he feels very strongly about their behavior. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these verses as if he were speaking directly to the people. Alternate translation: [is upon you people of Israel]
Here, **my nose** represents “my anger.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and I am sending my anger on you]

Yahweh is using **I will place on you all of your abominations** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will make you bear the consequences of all of your abominations.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. 4.note: Yahweh is using **my eyes will not pity you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will not show you any compassion.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Yahweh is using **I will place your ways on you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will punish you for how you have behaved.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will punish you for your conduct]

Similar to the previous phrase, Yahweh is using **your abominations will be in your midst** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will punish you for your abominations.” There is also the sense that, as part of the punishment, Yahweh will confront the Israelites with these abominations, of which they will be ashamed. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **abominations**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the horrible things that you have done]
The word **you** is plural here because Yahweh is now addressing the people of Israel rather than the land, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The implication is that when these things happen, the people will recognize that Yahweh is the true God, who has the power and authority to do what he has said he will do. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See the Introduction to Ezekiel for more information. Yahweh is using the adjective **mighty** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [mighty people]

The expression **will be defiled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to state who will do the action, the context indicates that the evil nations will do it. Alternate translation: [and they will defile their sanctuaries]

25.note: If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **Terror**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [The Israelites will soon be terrified]

The pronoun **they** refers to the people of Israel, not to the nations mentioned in the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Then the people of Israel will seek]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to be peaceful]

26.q: הֹוָ֤ה עַל הֹוָה֙ תָּב֔וֹא וּ⁠שְׁמֻעָ֥ה אֶל שְׁמוּעָ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶ֑ה
26.note: Yahweh is using **Disaster on disaster** and **rumor to rumor** as common expressions of the culture to mean “many disasters” and “many rumors.” If these phrases do not have that meaning for your readers, you could use comparable expressions from your language that do have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [One disaster after another will come, and there will be one rumor after another] or [many disasters will come, and there will be many rumors]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **prophet**. He means prophets in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [from any of the prophets]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **priest**. He means priests in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [from the priests]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if **the instruction** were a living thing that could **perish**. It means that the priests will no longer be able to teach the people what God wants. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and a priest will no longer give instruction]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the counsel will perish from elders]

27.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if **desolation** were clothing that **the prince** could **wear**. It means that the prince will feel great despair. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the prince will be completely without hope]

Yahweh is using **the hands** of the people to represent the people themselves. Hands that tremble show that a person is terrified. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the people of the land will be terrified] or [and the hands of the people of the land will tremble with fear]

The expression **will be terrified** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [will tremble]

The implication is that Yahweh will judge the people by the same standards that they used to judge other people. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and by the same standards that they used to judge other people, I will judge them]
